static_traits.name: Zhu Li
static_traits.social_status: Has friends at the art school, but finds it hard to discuss with them the unease and lack of confidence about the work
static_traits.medical_history: Has never received psychotherapy; no major physical illness; similar psychological problems only appeared after entering art school
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to reflect and cooperate; positive attitude; absolute and self-deprecating expressions often appear in the narration (such as 'I will never get better' and 'I should give up'); tends to personalize neutral/external events; easily ignores positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel I am a bad painter, and I attribute any negative event (such as my art teacher being sick and taking leave) to my own lack of skill; these feelings of inadequacy appeared after entering art school and have intensified in recent months, leading me to doubt my artistic ability in every situation, causing anxiety and self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize these negative thoughts are affecting my artistic growth and mental health, so I sought counseling, hoping to see events more clearly and to challenge and change the negative beliefs.
growth_experiences: After entering art school, a sense of self-inadequacy and anxiety began to appear and gradually worsened: in class or when receiving feedback, the automatic thought 'I am not good enough' frequently arose, and the client believed that any negative or incidental event was related to their own lack of ability; perfectionism and fear of failure became persistent sources of stress, gradually affecting progress in artistic creation, relationships with classmates and teachers, and sleep and self-care.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible painter / I am not good enough
If it is not perfect, it means failure

special_situations.event: 艺术老师因生病缺席课堂
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a negative or abnormal event occurs, it must be related to my lack of ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practicing twice as hard in pursuit of perfection, and constantly seeking others' approval to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The teacher took leave because I draw badly; it is all my fault

special_situations.event: Receiving constructive criticism from teachers or classmates in class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach a very high standard, it means I will never be good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Feels tense, avoidant, or overly defensive in feedback situations; practices desperately after class in an attempt to reach 'perfection'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never get better; I should give up

special_situations.event: In art class, making lateral comparisons with classmates' work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as good as my peers, I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing oneself with others, practicing twice as hard, and seeking external evaluation to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; my level is not enough

special_situations.event: Receiving positive evaluations/praise from classmates or teachers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive evaluations are unreliable; my shortcomings are the facts
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or negating positive feedback, only focusing on criticism to avoid making mistakes

core_conflict.wish: Longs for own artistic ability to be recognized and seen, obtaining genuine affirmation and acceptance
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying others will judge oneself as not good enough
defense_goal: Avoiding failure and humiliation through self-criticism and high standards
Stays vigilant about evaluation, denying positive feedback to maintain 'safe' boundaries of self-expectation

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough student / terrible painter who may fail at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: A critical judge (teacher/classmate) who will point out my shortcomings at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving positive feedback/praise from teachers or classmates in class
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously believes praise is unreal or merely perfunctory (transference: others are seen as untrustworthy judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Quickly negates or downplays praise, tone is brief, emphasizes shortcomings, and avoids discussing the positive side.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing constructive criticism, or when neutral / uncertain events occur (such as a teacher's absence)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Personalizes external events as their own fault, believing others hold negative evaluations of them (transference: others are seen as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses self-deprecating statements (such as 'it is all my fault' and 'I am not capable'), lowers speech rate and volume, shows guilt and shame, and weakens self-assertion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When comparing with classmates' work, or when self-evaluating academic success and failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views self and others in an all-good / all-bad manner, believing themselves 'never good enough' (transference: others are seen as always better / more valuable)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses absolute words (such as 'forever' and 'completely'), ignores middle ground and signs of progress, with a certain and negative tone.

manifestations: Although there are friends at the art school, finds it hard to talk to others about the unease and lack of confidence regarding the work
In classroom and feedback situations, experiences self-doubt and personalizes events, with inner experience trapped in self-criticism
outcomes: Strained relationships with classmates and teachers, limited interaction

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Taking perfection as the only standard, internalizing high external demands as self-demands
Rigid self-rules such as 'I should give up' appear
In feedback situations, using others' standards as the sole basis for judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: 频繁自我贬低与过度自责
When receiving criticism, quickly attributing the problem to oneself and falling into anxiety
Overly caring about others' opinions, difficulty evaluating by internal standards

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Interpreting the teacher's absence as dissatisfaction with one's work or as related to oneself
Without obtaining evidence, assumes others hold negative views of them (mind reading)

exception_events.target_problem: In group work or classroom feedback situations, the client usually presupposes that they perform the worst and engages in self-negation, leading to increased anxiety and avoidance of collaboration / feedback.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a group project, the client originally thought their own contribution was the worst, but peers actually gave praise; this time the client did not fall into the usual wholesale negation, and the result was positive feedback and a positive outcome different from expectations.
exception_events.reason: Clues: peers' positive feedback and a cooperative atmosphere enabled the client to see evidence different from their self-assumptions; in concrete tasks there were clear outputs and evaluations from others, resulting in a loosening of the negative automatic thoughts.

positive_force: Proactively seeking counseling to change thinking patterns
Willing to record and examine one's automatic thoughts (having reflective motivation)
In peer collaboration, able to receive the support of positive feedback
Able to recognize and name own negative patterns (such as overgeneralization, personalization)
negative_force: 完美主义与对失败的恐惧
Excessively seeking external validation, ignoring internal standards
Personalizes neutral/external events and attributes them to oneself

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-deprecation and anxiety in art class and feedback situations
antecedent: Receiving criticism or suggestions from teachers/classmates
Uncertain or neutral events such as the art teacher being absent
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by perfectionism and fear of failure, personalizes external events and evaluates the self by all-or-nothing standards
target_behavior.function: Avoids shame and negative evaluation; gains a temporary sense of control through self-criticism and seeking external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Artistic progress and creativity are blocked; relationships with classmates and teachers are strained; self-care and sleep are affected

target_behavior.behavior: Discounting or downplaying positive feedback (ignoring praise)
antecedent: Obtaining positive evaluation/praise from teachers or classmates in class or homework
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases engaged in to maintain the core belief 'I am not good enough', avoiding the anxiety brought by disappointed expectations
target_behavior.function: Maintaining internal consistency, reducing the sense of uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Confidence is hard to raise; persistent self-doubt and anxiety
